interest: Tracks the military's grip on Japanese government, from Stimson's 1933 remarks to the post-February 26 reform plan.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.01, spanning January 1933 to November 1937) documents U.S. State Department monitoring of Japanese government structures, administrative reform, and the creeping militarization of state machinery. The file begins with a 1933 document note recording Secretary of State Henry L. Stimson's warning to the Japanese Ambassador that the United States could not view Japan as a normal government as long as it remained under the sway of radical junior military officers. The core of the file consists of a November 1936 Tokyo Embassy despatch and State Department memorandum detailing joint recommendations by the Imperial Japanese Army and Navy to centralize executive authority under the Prime Minister, consolidate domestic and colonial ministries, and renovate the Imperial Diet. The collection concludes with late 1937 documentation referencing Ambassador Joseph C. Grew's reports on restructuring Japan's governmental machinery to establish a complete wartime footing.
